title: StepUp GP – A Multimodal Intervention to Promote Physical Activity Among Patients in Geriatric Psychiatry Day Clinics: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study
summary:
Gerontopsychiatric care focuses in particular on severe mental illnesses such as dementia, depression, and schizophrenia, which are associated with significant limitations in quality of life, everyday activities, and physical health (Berry, K.; Barrowclough, 2008; Liegert et al., 2024). Exercise is an important part of a healthy lifestyle. Studies show that regular physical activity can improve mood, reduce the risk of physical illness, increase overall well-being, and promote drive and mental performance. However, it can be difficult for people with mental illnesses such as depression
or schizophrenia to stay sufficiently active. We therefore want to investigate whether specifically promoting exercise by tracking step counts can help people become more active in the long term and feel better. Pedometers, smartwatches, and smartphones help people visualize their own exercise. They show how many steps a person takes each day and can motivate them to exercise a little more than usual. In this study, we want to find out whether tracking steps and specifically promoting physical activity can help increase activity in everyday life. To do this, we record the average number of steps per day and use this to set an individual weekly step goal. You try to achieve this goal every day and document your daily steps in a step tracking diary provided.
conditions: Older semi-inpatient patients in geriatric psychiatric care, without cognitive impairment, with diagnoses such as F30–F39 – Affective disorders, schizophrenia/psychotic disorders  F20 – Schizophrenia  F23 – Acute transient psychotic disorders  F25 – Schizoaffective disorders; personality and behavioral disorders (non-organic) F 60 - 68; anxiety, obsessive-compulsive, stress, and somatoform disorders F40 - 48, behavioral syndromes associated with physical functions F50 - 54

interventions.name: Upon admission to the geriatric psychiatric day clinic, patients who are undergoing treatment for a mental illness and who may meet the inclusion criteria are informed about the study verbally and in writing and asked if they would like to participate. All interested participants are then assessed f

The screening and recruitment process is the same as for the intervention group.

Control group:
Patients in the control group focus on their sleep and record it in a sleep diary. After the initial testing, patients take part in a health workshop. They also receive a diary to record their sleep.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients at geriatric psychiatric day clinics with a psychiatric diagnosis, ability to provide a signed consent form, mild cognitive impairment (Mini Mental Status Test ≥ 20), ability to stand for at least 3 minutes without assistance (self-assessment)
Exclusion criteria:
F22.0 Isolated delusional disorders, mobility, cognitive, sensory, and/or psychiatric impairments or comorbidities that affect the ability to participate and/or perform pre- and post-examinations, insufficient knowledge of the German language to participate in the health lecture and/or record activities, immobility, wheelchair dependency
